prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [反例] 交错跨列 · 共享中间列 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "与业务方共同梳理核心流程，输出需求说明书并完成评" spans 2 col × 1 row; "完成核心模块开发与联调，接入统一认证与日志平台" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 35px
  col 2: header "阶段一" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 87px
  col 3: header "阶段二" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "阶段三" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 53px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 199px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 198px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 199px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated poor: 各列表头和项目名称均逐字竖排；“搭建脚手架”也被压成六行，开发行显得狭长。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 阶段一较宽，“搭建脚手架”和“用例”更易读；两处跨列长文本也能形成相对连贯的文本块。但项目列和阶段三仍然过窄。 | another layout was rated poor: 跨列的开发说明较紧凑，但阶段一中的“搭建脚手架”和“用例”逐字换行，影响该列的扫描。 | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: “阶段二”表头保持一行，跨列开发说明也较紧凑；但阶段一过窄，使“搭建脚手架”和“用例”逐字换行。 | another layout was rated poor: 阶段一内容逐字换行，项目列和多个表头也很狭窄；跨列文本虽较紧凑，整行仍显拥挤。 | another layout was rated poor: 项目列、各阶段表头和“搭建脚手架”都逐字换行，两段长说明也形成偏长的文本块。
your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: 两个跨列说明的行数较少，但阶段一列很窄，“搭建脚手架”和“用例”被逐字拆开；阶段二表头占一行，与相邻表头的节奏不一致。 | another layout was rated poor: 阶段一和阶段二都过窄，表头和短词多处逐字换行；两段跨列说明也较长，行高偏大。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 跨列说明比较紧凑，但阶段一列的“搭建脚手架”和“用例”逐字排列，影响纵向扫读。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 跨列说明的换行较紧凑，但阶段一列仍过窄，短词被拆成单字，表头的换行也不均衡。 | another layout was rated good: 阶段一和阶段二有更宽的文字空间，“用例”和“回归”各占一行，“搭建脚手架”也更易读；第二段跨列说明稍长，但整体行列关系清晰。 | another layout was rated poor: 中间列较窄，表头、短词和两段跨列说明频繁换行，使表格偏高，比较各阶段较费力。
